sections.content:
25,985 people

were counted on the census as "data entry administrators" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Data entry administrators enter a variety of information into databases using various software packages and assist colleagues in retrieving information.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "data entry administrators" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "data entry administrators", 14.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "data entry administrators" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "data entry administrators" included:

  • human resources administrative occupations
  • vehicle and parts salespersons and advisers
  • sales administrators

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "data entry administrators" there were a similar number of men and women (45.2% compared with 54.8%).

This means "data entry administrators" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "administrative occupations".

Men made up 45.2% and women made up 54.8% of "data entry administrators"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "data entry administrators" included:

  • information technology trainers
  • business and related research professionals
  • estate agents and auctioneers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "data entry administrators" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "data entry administrators" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "data entry administrators", 12.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (74.6% compared with 25.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (95.8%) than self-employed (4.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
